article.summary: CLIO is a Perl terminal agent with project-scoped long-term memory, session key/value notes, searchable session history, and context recovery. Its source describes explicit memory writes, lexical relevance scoring, trust corroboration, and local persistence. This is a source review; no runtime or benchmark results were collected.

who_what.text: The catalog identifies CLIO, slug clio, and lists the repository with explicit locator status. It attributes the roster entry to the pinned Atlas report; Atlas was used for identity and locator attribution only.

The official repository is public and names main as the default branch. Its main feed reports full head 4babd7be9dc15acc894d4089ff4eb840ad3e10cf updated 2026-11-17T23:53:30Z; the repository page shows the matching abbreviated head.
The official README describes CLIO as a Perl terminal agent and extensible harness. The memory guide documents local project and session state, rather than a hosted memory service.

architecture.text: The documented memory design combines STM, a sliding active message window; YaRN, a durable session thread archive with compressed summaries; and project-level LTM. Separate operations provide session key/value notes and transcript search.

LTM stores discoveries, problem-solution pairs, code patterns, workflows, failures, and context rules in JSON with metadata. Entries can carry confidence, timestamps, examples, counts, and corroboration state. PathResolver maps a project UUID from .clio/project_uuid to data under ~/.clio/projects/<uuid>/.

The context builder scores memories against the current request, active task, and unresolved state, then places selected items in dynamic context. Session transcript recall and key/value retrieval are distinct tool operations.

behavior.text: Write: agents explicitly call add_discovery, add_solution, or add_pattern for significant knowledge. LTM persistence uses atomic writes; session working notes use separate key/value operations.

Update: update_ltm replaces matching entry text. A rewritten entry resets to unverified and clears prior corroboration identities and count. The inspected sources do not establish automatic correction behavior for arbitrary transcript messages.

Delete: session memory supports delete by key. The exposed LTM maintenance operation prunes old or low-confidence entries with tier-specific retention, but the reviewed tool contract has no direct delete-by-entry operation. Complete erasure from backups or every copy is not established.

Retrieval: ContextBuilder uses lexical keyword overlap, a relevance threshold, confidence floor, and a maximum of five injected LTM entries. recall_sessions returns scored matches from previous session histories; session key/value records can be retrieved, searched, or listed. No answer-level abstention or citation guarantee was identified.

Scope: project data directories are keyed by project UUID resolved from .clio/project_uuid. The path resolver documents the launch directory as the project root and explicit project boundaries. This source inspection did not verify isolation with runtime boundary tests.

Provenance and evidence: LTM corroboration is attributed to distinct agent:session identities and can promote trust tier; the runtime tool constrains supplied identity to active runtime identity. This supports an origin/corroboration record, not claim-level citations or proof that a generated answer follows from a memory.

Efficiency and observability: persistence uses local files and atomic writes; LTM selection is bounded and the tool exposes statistics. Context management uses token estimates and a bounded projection. These are documented/source-visible design choices, not measured results.

limits.text: This is a bounded inspection of the official README, memory guide, LTM store, memory tool, context builder, and project path resolver at one verified SHA; it does not cover every integration, migration, or failure mode.

No CLIO runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was run. Runtime reliability, recall quality, correction quality, deletion completeness, project isolation under edge cases, and all metric values remain unknown.
The documentation describes trust promotion, pruning, and recovery; these behaviors were not verified by execution for this review.
No direct LTM item deletion operation was found in the inspected tool contract. Complete erasure from backups or every persisted copy remains unknown.
Corroboration records distinct agent/session identity but does not establish the truth of stored content or provide claim-level citations.
